evidence: src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts: constructor(private readonly orders: OrderRepository) uses orders.findById and orders.save, which are port methods only
src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts: depends on OrderRepository and StockReservationService. It calls order.cancel(), stock.release(order.lines), then orders.save(order)
src/application/GetStockLevelsUseCase.ts: products.findAll() via ProductRepository, mapped with toStockLevelDto
src/application/ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.ts: reuses domain isOrderStatus and does not write its own copy of the status check
src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: builds lines with OrderLine.create, persists through orders.save and reserves stock through StockReservationService
src/application/dto.ts: toOrderDto and toStockLevelDto are the only mapping definitions, and every use case calls them
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/application module passes. All six files serve one concern: order and stock use cases that go through domain ports and map results to DTOs. Every use case reaches persistence only through the module's repository ports, OrderRepository and ProductRepository, which are injected through the constructors. No file imports or uses a database, ORM or query client directly. All output mapping goes through the shared toOrderDto and toStockLevelDto in dto.ts, so the module's DTO abstraction is used consistently. ListOrdersByStatusUseCase calls the domain's isOrderStatus instead of writing its own copy of the status check. The same order-not-found guard appears in both AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase. It is a standard check that the repository lookup found a record, not a copied business rule or invariant, so I don't count it as duplication. PlaceOrderUseCase checks the customer id inline. I can't see whether the Order constructor repeats that check, because domain source isn't included, so it isn't counted as a violation. No candidate flags were raised.
